body.x: A sketch on a screen seldom shows how a chair, a shoe or a room will look at full size, yet design teams have to agree on a direction before detailed engineering begins.
Closing that gap means letting designers sketch an idea in 3D space, test color and material options with AI, and review the result at full scale with their team in a virtual room.

Overay Inc., an extended reality (XR) software company founded in July 2022 and led by CEOs Kyungmin So and Sukhyun Seo, develops productivity and creative solutions built on spatial computing. Its flagship product, Overay Design, combines VR-based 3D sketching, AI-powered design concept generation and collaborative reviews in virtual environments in one workflow. Overay is exhibiting the tool at KES 2026.

Users draw ideas directly in 3D space, explore variations in color, material and finish (CMF) with AI, and compare the form and proportions of a product at full scale. Overay Design complements existing detailed design workflows by supporting early-stage concept exploration, design reviews and discussions on revisions, so a team can share an understanding of a designer's vision and decide on a direction from clearly visualized concepts.

A beta version of Overay Design is available through a global app store, and the company is preparing an official launch in 2026. It is improving features and usability based on feedback from professional designers and users, while running pilot trials and adoption talks with companies and educational institutions. Overay secured seed funding from BonAngels Venture Partners in November 2023 and was selected for the Deep Tech TIPS Fast Track program in November 2024.

The company already sells Overay Desk, its XR productivity solution, to international customers and operates that service globally. For Overay Design, it plans to add a web-based collaboration service connected to its VR app, offered as software as a service (SaaS), so designers in different countries can develop and review ideas together. Its overseas targets are individual designers, companies and educational institutions across design fields, and it wants support with translating and localizing educational content and with digital marketing abroad.

At KES 2026, Overay is looking for partners for joint proof-of-concept (PoC) projects in product, furniture, footwear, automotive, spatial and interior design. With companies, it plans to test the tool in developing product and spatial concepts, reviewing forms and proportions, and deciding on design directions as a team. With educational institutions, it wants to support classroom practice in which students express ideas in 3D and examine their own designs from different angles.

The goal is to move beyond demonstrations and learn what the tool contributes to everyday design work and teaching. Overay plans to use the results to support regular adoption and educational programs, build domestic use cases and an initial customer base, and use them as a foundation for international expansion.

KES 2026, the 57th Korea Electronics Show, runs Oct. 13 to Oct. 16 at COEX Halls A and B in Seoul. The show features X-SPACE 2026, a special exhibition on spatial computing that covers XR content creation tools, virtual simulation and digital twins, and its KES Match program arranges meetings with domestic buyers from Oct. 14 to Oct. 16.
